# Document Preparation Functions

Provides document preparation, provider submission, admission and readiness functions, with neutral domain-specific hooks. It supports constructing a document from a configured template or requesting an existing initialized document that satisfies the prepared requirements. These are callable functions; their presence does not establish a caller’s permission or an automatic execution schedule.

## Domain hooks

- `domainPrepare(prepared)` returns `{}`, stored as `domainTerms`: this type adds no domain-specific frozen terms.
- `domainValidateCandidate(candidate, frozenTerms)` returns `true`: this type adds no domain-specific rejection, but inherited preparation checks still apply.
- `domainNextActions(documentRef)` returns `[]`: this type supplies no domain-specific follow-up actions. During refresh, `documentRef` contains the selected document’s `documentOrigin` and `path`.

The `checkedDomain*` wrappers reject hooks that change the changeset or event counts, or return the wrong result kind. Next-action results must be a list of at most 16 `Clause Response` descriptions; emitted actions must name a declared party.

## Preparation and configuration

`preparePublic(input)` accepts `key`, `requestId`, `fields` and `values`. The key must be nonempty text; its processing default is `single`, and singleton preparation permits only that key. `prepareKeyedPublic` requires an explicit nonempty key. `requestId` defaults to the resolved key and must also be nonempty text. Omitted `fields` and `values` become empty objects in the recorded intent; supplied content must fit the configured template.

Execution requires a nonempty `bindings.parties` mapping. `cardinality` and `destinationBinding` come from `/clauses/{clauseKey}/type`: the latter names the binding containing the destination path. Singleton preparation uses that path directly; collection preparation appends the escaped key. An occupied destination is rejected when no preparation entry exists. An existing entry with different intent is rejected; intent includes configuration and template identities, `requestId`, `fields` and `values`. Although the check labels matching intent `duplicate`, `sharedPrepare` still constructs, records and emits preparation, so this is not a general guarantee of side-effect-free retries.

Configuration parameter `obtain` defaults to `create` and permits only `create` or `provide`:

- `create` writes the prepared document to the destination and records `documentOrigin` with status `selected`. Nonempty `suppliedParties` is rejected.
- `provide` records `awaiting_provider` and requires nonempty `suppliedBy`, stored as `supplier`. It emits `Document Provision Requested` with `party`, `inResponseTo`, `requirementRef`, `clauseId` and `itemKey`.

Both modes emit `Document Prepared`. `requirementRef` identifies the prepared document and its requirements; it is not confirmation that a provider has fulfilled them.

## Provider submission

`providePublic(input)` takes `key` (default `single`), an existing initialized `document`, `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`. The preparation must exist, use `obtain: provide`, and match both references. `call/channel` must equal `supplier`. Statuses `reapproval_required`, `admission_denied`, `cancelled` and `cancellation_requested` reject provision.

The candidate’s original document is read from `/contracts/initialized/document`. Outside permitted specialization slots, its normalized original must match the prepared document. Its effective clause policy must also match, including clause types, parameters, bindings and any names or descriptions. The activation approval requirements must remain unchanged.

Party slots come from the template’s activation party declarations. `suppliedParties` defaults to `[]` and identifies roles the provider may fill; other roles must preserve the prepared main party. Original and current parties must satisfy their constraints and pass main-party identity checks. Undeclared parties are rejected, and corresponding party transport declarations must match their lead channels.

`specialization/dataPaths` defaults to `[]`. Each path must identify an existing data slot, begin with `/`, and neither duplicate nor overlap another slot. Reserved top-level paths include `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `sources`, `type`, `blueId`, `instanceKey`, `creationIntent` and `preparationContext`. Original and current data must satisfy the configured constraint and remain identical between initialization and submission.

A staged candidate records `candidateOrigin` and `candidateRef`; a different candidate origin cannot replace it. A selected `documentOrigin` likewise cannot be replaced. Passing validation can still leave the entry `admission_pending`, `awaiting_activation` or `linking`. Only a stage of `ready` leads to writing the candidate reference at the destination, recording `selected`, and emitting `Document Selected`.

## Admission

When `bindings.sources` contains `self`, candidate parties missing from the executing document’s roster require admission. This requires configured `/clauses/activation/parameters/admission/approvers` and the required Timeline Access documents. The admission token binds the candidate, requirements, missing parties, access scope, activation revision and attempt; `admissionRef` identifies that token.

Admission requires an approved matching grant, each added party’s explicit `approve`, a current activation revision and valid access. Consent operations use each party’s lead channel. They reject stale or wrong admission references, invalid decisions and changes to a final decision; repeating the same decision returns `duplicate`. A decline produces `admission_denied`; a changed activation revision requires reapproval.

`Party Addition Requested` requests access-document installation and can precede complete consent. It does not itself grant private timeline access, supply consent or confirm admission. Installation proceeds through `installing`; `finishAdmission` verifies roster coverage, records `admittedRevision`, changes status to `linking`, and emits admission progress with status `admitted`.

`rebaseAdmissionPublic` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion: true`, an admission approver’s channel, the current `admissionRef`, and status `reapproval_required`. It clears the old token, reference and consents, increments `admissionAttempt`, and returns the entry to `awaiting_provider`, emitting `reprovision_required`. The candidate identity remains fixed.

## State, readiness and cancellation

Entries reside at `/process_{clauseKey}/entries/{key identity}` in the executing document. Each entry records its destination `path`, correlation and requirement references, prepared content, specialization slots and lifecycle status. Missing state is unknown, not evidence of completion or a configuration default.

`sharedRefresh` checks selected documents with an initialized original and rejects changed origin identity. It marks an entry `usable` only when the selected document’s `/activation/active` is exactly `true` and its named sources are ready; otherwise it records `selected`. Source readiness requires initialized sources with the declared origins, active status and roster coverage by matching lead channels and nonempty matching reader-key sets. A nonempty `selectionPath` additionally requires the source’s selected process to identify this document. No declared source requirements makes the source check succeed. Transition to `usable` emits `Document Attached`; readiness can subsequently fall back to `selected`.

`cancelPublic` accepts `key`, defaulting to `single`. It requires an existing entry without `documentOrigin`; selected processes require domain cancellation. It records `cancellation_requested` and emits `Preparation Cancellation Requested`; repeating that request returns `duplicate`. This does not establish completed cancellation.

Detailed template construction and some inherited access and identity checks are not specified here; successful local requests do not establish external completion.
